name: Sand Brown
lede: Sand Brown is a dusty, golden-tan color named for dry sand, one of the most common colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A landscape word, not a modifier
sections.body:
Our graph files this as a landscape word in its own right rather than a modifier of another name, recorded by the 2010 xkcd crowd survey [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists call its block a "dark yellow" [1]. In Munsell terms it sits near 1.5Y 6.9/6.2 [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[sand-yellow]], [[olive-ocher]] and [[roe]], at 2.6, [[tan|Tan]] and [[khaki|Khaki]] sit close by in the same family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Sand Brown is one of the most common colors in our archive: it covers at least 2% of the canvas in 2,092 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. By its position in each painting's lightness order it is found in 1,558, more common than 94% of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1300s, at nearly three times the archive's baseline rate, and is most over-represented in [[painter:francisco-de-zurbaran|Francisco de Zurbarán]]'s work, 25 times his museums' baseline across 10 of his 40 paintings here [2].

[[painter:fritz-thomsen|Fritz Thomsen]] carries it even more densely, in 6 of his 18 works, and [[painter:john-singer-sargent|John Singer Sargent]] has it in 19 of his 287 [2]. The earliest match is 1150, 860 years before the name's own 2010 record, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof anyone named or mixed it that way then, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
